hint.saved: Saved records are written to PostgreSQL and recorded in the audit trail.
hint.existing: Choose one to load it back into the form, or leave blank to create.
hint.issued_on_save: Issued when it is first saved.
hint.locked: :no is :status — it can no longer be changed here.
hint.loan_opening_list: One position per party per item, carrying both directions — a party that lent us some and borrowed some back has one net account, not two.
hint.loan_opening: Needles already out on loan when the register opens.
hint.category: Narrows the item list below it. The position is held against the item.
hint.loan_received: Lent to us by this party, and not yet given back.
hint.loan_issued: Lent by us to this party, and not yet returned.
hint.cost_price: What the needles were valued at when the book opened.
hint.is_final: Both sides have agreed the figure. A finalised position stops being editable.
hint.opening_list: Every opening sheet, per store and date. A finalised sheet is in the book and can no longer be changed.
hint.opening: Pick the company, the store and the opening date, press Load, and the store's needles come up with whatever has already been entered against them.
hint.ob_category: Narrows the grid. Leave it blank to type a whole shelf at once.
hint.ob_load: Pick a company, a store and an OB date, then press Load. The sheet is per store and per date, because that is what the count was of.
hint.ob_zero: A line left at zero is not stored — a zero opening and no row at all are the same fact. Load re-reads the sheet from the database.
hint.ob_finalized: This sheet is finalised: its stock is in the book and it can no longer be changed.
hint.assign_list: Every unit and category with machines fitted. A finalised fit is the machine's standard and can no longer be changed.
hint.assign: Pick a unit and a category, press Load, and every machine on that unit comes up with the item it is fitted with and how many.
hint.assign_load: Pick a unit and a category, then press Load. One row per machine within a category — a machine's needle and its sinker are two loads of this screen.
hint.fit_zero: A machine left with no item or a quantity of zero is not assigned — clearing the box is how a fit is taken off.
hint.fit_finalized: This fit is finalised: it is the machines' standard and can no longer be changed.
hint.closing: Show Exception lists what would stop the close without changing anything. Start Closing applies the same checks again and strikes the month if they pass — a store with unfinalised paper in the window is skipped rather than closed over.
hint.closing_date: The month this date falls in is the one Start Closing strikes. Leave it blank to strike each store's next due month.
hint.receipt_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent receipts. Item Name matches the needle code as well as its description, because the store quotes the part number.
hint.receipt_form: Fill in the delivery and the paper it came on, list the needles under it, and saving books the receipt in as a draft.
hint.receipt_store: The needle store the delivery was taken into.
hint.lc_no: An import only. A local receipt has no letter of credit behind it.
hint.receipt_lines: One line per needle or sinker. Challan Qty is what the supplier's paper claimed; Received Qty is what the store counted — they disagree often enough to be worth both.
hint.receipt_status: Draft — verified and approved from the receive list.
hint.receipt_foot: Saving writes a draft. Verify, Accounts Approve and Finalize on the list are what move it; Verify is the store counting it in, and once it has left the store's desk the lines can no longer be changed here.
hint.consumption: What the store took in and let go of, needle by needle, between two dates. Every column is summed from the documents themselves.
hint.consumption_store: Pick a store, then press Show. The board is per store, because a needle sitting on one shelf is not stock on another.
hint.return_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent return challans. A challan is raised from the receipt it answers — either from the Raise Return button on the receive list, or on the entry desk beside this one.
hint.return_form: Pick the delivery the needles came in on, trim the quantities going back, and saving writes the challan as a draft.
hint.return_mrr: A return always answers a receipt — pick one on the left and its lines come across.
hint.rtn_challan: Left blank, the desk numbers it after the receipt — NMR-…-R01.
hint.return_type: Returnable means the goods are expected back through the gate — sent for servicing, or swapped.
hint.return_lines: The receipt's outstanding lines. Trim Return Qty to what is actually going back — a line set to zero is left alone.
hint.return_status: Draft — issued at the gate and finalised from the return list.
hint.return_foot: Saving writes a draft. Issue at Gate is what moves the store's balance, and it is on the list — the receipt's returned quantity moves with it, so the two can never disagree.
hint.broken_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent shifts. Qty and Cost Price are summed from the machines on each record, so a line corrected on the entry desk moves both.
hint.broken_form: Say which unit, machine type, date and shift the sheet covers, list the machines that broke needles on it, and saving writes the record as a draft.
hint.office_machines: Narrows the machine list on the grid below.
hint.machine_type: Left blank when the sheet covers a mixed floor.
hint.broken_lines: One line per machine and needle. A machine that broke a cylinder needle and a sinker on the same shift has two lines.
hint.broken_status: Draft — confirmed from the breakage list.
hint.broken_foot: Saving writes a draft. Confirm on the list is the supervisor signing the count, and a machine-wise requisition can only be raised against a confirmed record.
hint.req_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent requisitions. Rqd, Iss and Balance are summed from the lines, so an issue raised on the issue list moves all three at once.
hint.req_form: Say which store is asking which, why, and against what breakage; list the machines and the needles they need, and saving writes the requisition as a draft.
hint.broken_confirmed: Confirmed records only. A store replacing against an unsigned count is replacing against a number nobody has agreed.
hint.from_store: The store raising the request — usually the unit's sub-store.
hint.to_store: The store being asked to release the needles — usually the main store.
hint.req_lines: One line per machine and needle. Iss.Qty is not on this grid: what is released is written on the issue desk, against this requisition.
hint.req_status: Draft — submitted and verified from the requisition list.
hint.req_foot: Saving writes a draft. Submit and Verify on the list are what move it; once it has been verified the lines can no longer be changed here, and what is released against it is written on the issue desk.
hint.issue_list: Every issue raised against a verified requisition, with the requisition's standing beside it. Withdraw takes a release back off the book.
hint.issue_form: Pick the requisition being answered, trim what is actually being released, and saving writes the issue and moves the requisition's Iss.Qty with it.
hint.issue_req: An issue always answers a requisition — pick one on the left and its outstanding lines come across.
hint.issue_lines: The requisition's outstanding lines. Trim Iss.Qty to what the store is actually releasing — a line set to zero is left owing.
hint.issue_status: Issued — the requisition's Iss.Qty moves with this document.
hint.issue_foot: Saving an issue moves the requisition's Iss.Qty and its status in the same transaction, so the two can never disagree. Withdrawing an issue takes the release back off.
hint.loan_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent requisitions. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines, so a line corrected on the desk moves all three at once.
hint.loan_form: Fill in who is asking and what for, list the needles under it, and saving writes the requisition as a draft.
hint.kind: Which way the needles are going. It cannot be changed once the requisition is saved.
hint.loan_store: The needle store being asked to release them.
hint.loan_lines: One line per needle or sinker. Issue Qty is what the store has actually released against the line — leave it at zero until it has.
hint.loan_status: Draft — submitted and verified from the requisition list.
hint.loan_issuing: Verified — only the Issue Qty column may be changed here; saving posts what the store has released.
hint.loan_foot: Saving writes a draft. Submit and Submit & Verify on the list are what move it; once it is verified only the Issue Qty column may be changed here.
hint.lo_list_NEEDLE: Needles requisitioned to be lent out to a party, and what it still owes. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines; Returned is what the party has handed back on received return challans.
hint.lo_list_OIL: Oil requisitioned to be lent out to a party, and what it still owes. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines; Returned is what the party has handed back on received return challans.
hint.lo_form_NEEDLE: Fill in who is asking and what for, list the needles under it, and saving writes the requisition as a draft.
hint.lo_form_OIL: Fill in the party the oil is being lent to, list what is going out, and saving writes the requisition as a draft.
hint.lo_store_OIL: The store being asked to release the oil.
hint.lo_lines_OIL: One line per oil. Issue Qty is what the store has actually released against the line — leave it at zero until it has.
hint.lb_list_NEEDLE: Nothing filled in loads the most recent return challans. RCV Date stays empty until the store counts the needles in — receiving is what fills it, and what puts the quantity back onto the requisition the loan went out on.
hint.lb_list_OIL: Nothing filled in loads the most recent return challans. RCV Date stays empty until the store measures the oil in — receiving is what fills it, and what puts the quantity back onto the requisition the loan went out on.
hint.lb_form: Fill in the party's return challan and list what came back on it. Saving writes the challan as a draft.
hint.lb_req_NEEDLE: The loan issue the needles went out on. Receiving the challan takes its quantity back off that requisition's balance.
hint.lb_req_OIL: The loan issue the oil went out on. Receiving the challan takes its quantity back off that requisition's balance.
hint.lb_receiver_NEEDLE: Who at the store counted the needles in. Required before the challan can be received.
hint.lb_receiver_OIL: Who at the store measured the oil in. Required before the challan can be received.
hint.lb_lines_NEEDLE: One line per needle or sinker coming back. Received Qty is what the store counted — leave it at zero and receiving the challan fills it in from the paper.
hint.lb_lines_OIL: One line per oil coming back. Received Qty is what the store measured — leave it at zero and receiving the challan fills it in from the paper.
hint.lb_status: Draft — received at the store and finalised from the return list.
hint.lb_foot_NEEDLE: Saving writes a draft. Receive at Store on the list is what counts the needles in, dates the challan and takes the quantity off what the party still owes.
hint.lb_foot_OIL: Saving writes a draft. Receive at Store on the list is what measures the oil in, dates the challan and takes the quantity off what the party still owes.
hint.lr_list_NEEDLE: Borrowed needles requisitioned to be sent back to the party they came from. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines.
hint.lr_list_OIL: Borrowed oil requisitioned to be sent back to the party it came from. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines.
hint.lr_form_NEEDLE: Fill in who is asking and what for, list the needles under it, and saving writes the requisition as a draft. Nothing more can go back than was borrowed from that party.
hint.lr_form_OIL: Fill in the party the borrowed oil is going back to, list what is being sent, and saving writes the requisition as a draft. Nothing more can go back than was borrowed from that party.
hint.lrc_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent receipts. Outstanding is what the factory has still to hand back — received less returned, line by line.
hint.lrc_form_NEEDLE: Fill in the challan the needles arrived on and list them under it. Saving writes the receipt as a draft.
hint.lrc_form_OIL: Fill in the challan the oil arrived on and list it under it. Saving writes the receipt as a draft.
hint.lrc_pay: Adjustment is the usual one: nothing changes hands, the quantity is squared against what the other side owes.
hint.lrc_lines_NEEDLE: One line per needle or sinker borrowed. Returned Qty is what has since gone back to the lender — the register's Outstanding column is this less that.
hint.lrc_lines_OIL: One line per oil borrowed. Returned Qty is what has since gone back to the lender — the register's Outstanding column is this less that.
hint.lrc_status: Draft — verified by the store and approved by accounts from the receive list.
hint.lrc_foot: Saving writes a draft. Submit, Verify and Accounts Approve on the list are what move it — Verify is the store counting it in. An L/C number belongs on an import and is refused on a local receipt.
hint.loan_opening_OIL: Oil already out on loan when the register opens. One position per party per item, carrying both directions — a party that lent us some and borrowed some back has one net account, not two.
hint.cost_price_OIL: What the oil was valued at when the book opened.
hint.oil_req_list: Oil asked for by the floor against machine running hours. Required, Issued and Balance are summed from the lines, so a line corrected on the desk moves all three at once.
hint.oil_req_form: Fill in which store is asking which, list the oil under it, and saving writes the requisition as a draft.
hint.oil_issuing: Verified: only Issue Qty can change now. Saving it releases the oil from the store asked into the store asking.
hint.oil_to_store: The store being asked to release the oil.
hint.oil_req_lines: One line per oil. Issue Qty is what the store has actually released against the line — leave it at zero until it has.
hint.oil_req_status: Draft — submitted and verified from the requisition list
hint.oil_req_foot: Saving writes a draft. 13-Submit and 14-Verify & Submit R on the list are what move it; once it is verified only the Issue Qty column may be changed here.
hint.oil_opening_list: One line per store, item and opening date. Finalising is on the row and on the opening sheet tab — a finalised line stops being editable, because a starting point that can still move is not a starting point.
hint.oil_sheet: Load the store's opening lines, tick the ones the count agrees with, and Finalize All signs the page off.
hint.oil_ob_form: The oil stock a new period opens with, per grade and drum.
hint.oil_ob_final: This opening line is finalized — it can no longer be changed.
hint.oil_ob_category: Narrows the item list beside it. The balance is held against the item.
hint.oil_unit_price: What the supplier invoiced, in the currency beside it.
hint.oil_conv_rate: What that currency was worth in the ledger's own on the opening date.
hint.oil_cost_price: Struck on save from the two boxes above it, so a page reprinted after a rate change still shows the arithmetic it was signed on.
hint.oil_cons_list: Oil drawn per machine per day, against its running hours. Requisition Date matches one day exactly; From and To take a window. Qty is summed from the machine lines.
hint.oil_cons_form: Fill in the shift the sheet covers, list the machines that drew oil on it, and saving writes the sheet.
hint.oil_issue_by: Who at the store handed the oil over. Required before the sheet can be finalised.
hint.oil_cons_lines: One line per machine and oil. Running Hrs is what the machine ran on the shift — it is the denominator the floor reads consumption over.
hint.oil_cons_status: Open — finalised from the consumption list
hint.oil_cons_foot: One sheet per store, date and shift. Saving leaves it open; Finalize on the list is the supervisor signing for it — the oil leaves the store then, and a finalised sheet stops being editable.
hint.oil_receipt_list: Nothing filled in loads the most recent receipts. RCV Qty and Cond. Qty are summed from the lines; Exchangable/Returnable is what is left after anything already sent back.
hint.oil_receipt_form: Fill in the challan the drums arrived on and list what was measured in.
hint.oil_receipt_req_type: A receipt nobody can trace to a requisition is a receipt nobody can check a price against.
hint.oil_receipt_lines: One line per oil. Challan Qty is what the supplier's paper claimed and RCV Qty what the store measured; Cond. Qty is the part of it accepted pending a test result.
hint.oil_receipt_status: Draft — signed for by QC, the store and accounts from the receive list
hint.oil_receipt_foot: Saving writes a draft. Send to Next Desk, Finalize and Accounting Done on the list are what move it — Finalize is the store saying the lines are right, and the oil is booked in then. An L/C number belongs on an import and is refused on a local receipt.
hint.oil_return_list: Receipts reversed — wrong grade, short measure or leaking drums. Issuing a return challan is what takes its quantity off the receipt it was raised against.
hint.oil_return_form: Pick the receipt the oil came in on, list the lines going back, and saving writes the challan as a draft.
hint.oil_return_mrr: The receipt the oil came in on. Its company, store and supplier are copied onto the challan.
hint.oil_return_type: Returnable is oil going out that will come back — sent for testing, or swapped. Non-returnable is oil the supplier is credited for and keeps.
hint.oil_return_lines: One line per receipt line going back. The dropdown shows how much of each is still returnable after anything already sent.
hint.oil_return_status: Draft — issued and finalised from the return list
hint.oil_return_foot: The company, store and supplier come from the receipt. Issue on the list is what sends the drums out and takes their quantity off the receipt.

hint.knitting: Every report on this list is run against the same three boxes. Yarn Item narrows the yarn reports, YR Approve? narrows the requisition ones, and Date Type says which of a document's dates the window applies to.
hint.yarn-store: Every report here is dated. Leave both boxes blank for everything on file — a stock report ignores the dates, because a balance is as at now rather than over a period.
hint.gfs: Buyer A/C, Style/Order#, Production Type and Store narrow whichever of them the chosen report reads. A parameter a report does not take simply does not narrow it.
hint.qc: Fourteen boxes, all of them optional. Roll List Without Grey QC is the one report here that answers with rolls having no inspection at all, so the QC Status and QC Grade boxes do not narrow it.
hint.flatknit: The flat-knit floor counts in pieces; only the yarn requisition report is in kilograms. Req. Type narrows that one to Solid or Y/D.
hint.yarn-stock: Stock is struck from every document that has moved the line — opening balance, receipts, issues, returns, dyed-yarn receipts, party challans and approved adjustments. Alloc is what an open requisition has reserved; Stock is what is left free.
hint.grey-stock: Today Rcv. Qty counts what the store took in on the To date; Total Rcv. Qty is everything in the window. Due for Prod. Qty is the order's target less what the floor has knitted, so fabric still on the machine counts.
hint.daily-output: The DAY and NIGHT columns split on the mill's own 08:30 boundary, taken from the shift pattern a roll was logged under and from the time on the scale where there is none. A rejected roll is knitted but not production, so it is left out of both.

f.note: Note

hint.receipt_list: The grid opens on every challan booked in from an outside knitter, most recent first.
hint.receipt_form: Grey fabric — and collar or cuff — arriving from an outside knitter, booked against the party's own challan.
hint.rcv_no: Issued when the challan is first saved.
hint.party_out: The outside knitter the fabric came from.
hint.store_rcv: Where the fabric was put. Required before the challan can be received.
hint.receipt_lines: One line per roll or lot on the party's challan. Fabric is counted in kilograms; collar and cuff in pieces.
hint.receipt_foot: Saving writes a draft. Receiving it on the register is what books the fabric in and puts it on the QC worklist.
hint.qc: Only challans carrying collar or cuff appear here — those are the lines held for inspection.
hint.ret_list: The grid opens on this screen's own return challans, most recent first.

ret_form.OUT_HOUSE: Grey fabric going back to an outside knitter — against a rejection, or against fabric they sent in error.
ret_form.IN_HOUSE: Grey fabric returned within the in-house sub-contract arrangement — a movement between two floors of the same site.

hint.party_ret: The party the fabric is going back to.
hint.store_ret: The store the fabric is leaving.

against.OUT_HOUSE: The receive challan this fabric came in on, when the return answers one.
against.IN_HOUSE: The party's programme receipt this fabric was knitted against, when the return answers one.

hint.ret_lines: One line per roll or lot going back. Picking a roll fills the line in and lets the issue move it out of the store; a line with no roll is a quantity that moves nothing.
hint.ret_foot: Saving writes a draft. Issuing it on the register is what takes the rolls out of the store; until then the fabric has not moved.
hint.delivery_list: The grid opens on every delivery challan, most recent first.
hint.delivery_form: One paper for one lorry: the fabric going out, the collar and cuff going with it, and the party's unused yarn going back.
hint.party_delivery: The in-house party the fabric is being delivered to.
hint.fabric_lines: One line per roll going out. Picking a roll fills its fabric, shade, dia, gauge and net weight — correct the weight only if the gate weighed it differently.
hint.collar_lines: Collar and cuff going with the fabric, counted in pieces rather than kilograms.
hint.yarn_lines: The party's leftover yarn going back with the lorry — item, shade and lot, because that is how a store counts a cone.
hint.delivery_foot: Saving builds the challan. Issuing it on the register is what takes the rolls out of the store — until then the fabric has not moved.
hint.existing: Choose one to load it back into the form, or leave blank to create.
hint.locked: :no is :status, so it can no longer be edited here.

empty.receipts: No receive challan matches that search
empty.qc: No collar/cuff challan matches that search
empty.returns: No return challan matches that search
empty.deliveries: No delivery challan matches that search
empty.hint: Change the search above and load again.
empty.receipt_lines: A receive challan with no lines posts nothing, so at least one is required before this can be saved.
empty.return_lines: A return challan with no lines posts nothing, so at least one is required before this can be saved.
empty.fabric: No fabric on this challan yet. A delivery may carry collar/cuff or yarn alone, so this grid is allowed to stay empty.
empty.collar: No collar or cuff on this challan.
empty.yarn: No yarn going back on this challan.

done.receive: :no received — the fabric is in the store.
done.issue: :no issued — the rolls are out of the store.

v.challan_no: Challan# is required — it is the party's own number.
v.qty: Qty must be more than nothing.
v.no_receipt_lines: A receive challan with no lines posts nothing, so at least one is required before this can be saved.
v.no_return_lines: A return challan with no lines posts nothing, so at least one is required before this can be saved.
v.no_delivery_lines: A delivery challan with nothing on it — no fabric, collar/cuff or yarn — sends nothing.
v.challan_taken: The party's challan :no is already booked in.
v.store_first: Pick the store the fabric was put in before receiving the challan.
v.receipt_used: :no cannot be cancelled: some of its fabric has already left the store.
v.against_party: That receive is not this party's.
v.line_store: Line :n is not held in the chosen store.
v.roll_twice: Line :n takes a roll already on this challan.
v.line_over: Line :n takes more than the store holds (:have).
v.yarn_lot: Line :n needs the yarn lot going back.
v.yarn_party: Line :n's yarn is not this party's.
v.yarn_short: Yarn lot :lot no longer holds that much.

maintenance.plan_has_occurrences: :count occurrences have been generated from this plan, so it cannot be removed. Deactivate it instead, which stops new ones and leaves the history explainable.
maintenance.template_intro: A checklist a technician is handed at the machine. Published versions are frozen — a revision is a new draft that takes effect when it is published.
maintenance.template_created: Checklist created. Add the checks it should carry.
maintenance.draft_started: A new draft is open. It takes effect when you publish it.
maintenance.publish_confirm: Publish this version? The one in force is archived, and every work order that ran it keeps resolving the version it actually used.
maintenance.version_published: Published. New work orders will be handed this version.
maintenance.version_is_frozen: This version is published and cannot be changed. Start a revision instead.
maintenance.platform_template_read_only: This checklist is supplied by the platform and shared with every company, so it cannot be edited.
maintenance.safety_hint: A safety check demands a photo and a note when it fails, and raises corrective work by itself. A tick in a box is not a record of a guard that was missing.
maintenance.name: Name
maintenance.label: Check
maintenance.seeded_hint: Provided with the system. Clone it to make changes.
maintenance.no_templates_hint: The system ships with templates for sewing, cutting, generators, boilers and compressors.
maintenance.no_items: This version has no items yet
maintenance.no_checklists_hint: Write one so a factory floor stops running against a checklist meant for a different machine.
maintenance.templates_page_description: What a technician actually works through — versioned, so a published one is frozen the moment it's signed against.
maintenance.code_readonly_hint: Ties every version together — never editable.
maintenance.platform_checklist_hint: A platform checklist — shared with every tenant, editable by none. Clone it to write your own wording.
maintenance.version_frozen: Version :version is published and cannot be edited. Create a new version instead, so historical work orders keep the checklist they were executed against.
maintenance.checklist_empty: A checklist needs at least one item.
maintenance.cannot_publish_empty: A checklist with no items cannot be published.
maintenance.needs_one_required_item: A checklist needs at least one required item. With none, a work order can be completed without a single answer.
maintenance.only_drafts_publish: Only a draft can be published; this version is :status.
maintenance.draft_already_open: Version :version is already an open draft. Finish or publish it first.
maintenance.item_type_unknown: Item :position has an unknown input type.
maintenance.tolerance_needs_numeric: Item :position sets a tolerance but is not a numeric check. The tolerance would be ignored at execution.
maintenance.tolerance_inverted: Item :position has a minimum above its maximum.
maintenance.choice_needs_options: Item :position is a choice but lists no options.
maintenance.delete_plan_hint: Only possible while the plan has never generated an occurrence.
maintenance.plans_page_description: The rules that turn a machine's calendar into scheduled work.
maintenance.target_asset_hint: Exactly one of asset or asset type — never both, never neither.
maintenance.requires_shutdown_checkbox: Requires the machine to be shut down
maintenance.schedule_page_description: What's due, overdue, skipped, or already completed.
maintenance.non_working_day: If it falls on a non-working day
maintenance.no_plans_hint: A plan decides when a machine is serviced. Create one to start generating work.
maintenance.no_schedules_hint: Occurrences appear here once a plan is activated.
maintenance.preview_hint: A dry run. Nothing is saved until you submit.
maintenance.preview_needs_interval: Set an interval to see the dates.
maintenance.preview_rolling_note: A rolling plan has one occurrence outstanding at a time. This preview assumes each is completed exactly on its due date; in practice the next date shifts with the actual completion.
maintenance.plan_created: Plan :name created. Activate it when you are ready to generate work.
maintenance.plan_activated: Plan :name is active and generating occurrences.
maintenance.plan_deactivated: Plan :name deactivated. Existing occurrences are left in place.
maintenance.plan_needs_rules: A plan needs at least one trigger rule before it can be activated.
maintenance.plan_already_ended: This plan is past its end date.
maintenance.target_exactly_one: A plan applies either to one machine or to every machine of a type. Choose exactly one.
maintenance.interval_required: A calendar trigger needs an interval.
maintenance.meter_threshold_required: A meter trigger needs a meter and a threshold.
maintenance.rule_logic_required: Choose whether either condition triggers the work, or both are required. There is no sensible default: they are different maintenance regimes.
maintenance.template_must_be_published: Only a published checklist version can be attached. A draft could still change underneath the plan.
maintenance.skip_needs_reason: A skipped service is a compliance exception, so it needs a reason.
maintenance.schedule_completed: Marked complete. The next occurrence has been generated.

masterdata.intro: The reference lists the rest of the system is written in. The platform supplies a starter set for the garment industry; anything your company adds is your own.
masterdata.import_hint: These lists can also be filled from a spreadsheet. Import writes the same rows this screen does, so use whichever suits the number of them.
masterdata.empty_hint: Add the first entry with the form beside this list, or import a spreadsheet of them.
masterdata.delete_confirm: Remove this entry? Only an entry nothing is filed against can be removed; anything in use must be deactivated instead.
masterdata.copied_hint: Copied from a platform entry. Give it a code of its own — two entries cannot share one.
masterdata.platform_row_read_only: This entry is supplied by the platform and shared with every company, so it cannot be edited. Add your own entry instead.
masterdata.code_taken: That code is already in use in this list.
masterdata.unknown_reference: That selection is not available to your company.
masterdata.in_use: This entry is used by :count records and cannot be removed. Deactivate it instead so it stops appearing in new work.
masterdata.self_parent: An entry cannot be its own parent.
masterdata.hierarchy_cycle: That parent sits underneath this entry, which would make a loop.
masterdata.hierarchy_too_deep: Only :levels levels are allowed: category, sub-category, detail category.
masterdata.same_unit_conversion: A unit cannot be converted to itself.
masterdata.delete_entry_description: Only possible while nothing points at it.

descriptions.buildings: The buildings on a factory site.
descriptions.departments: Sewing, knitting, dyeing, finishing, utility — how the factory is organised.
descriptions.sections: A narrower grouping inside a department.
descriptions.production-lines: The line a machine stands on, which is how a floor supervisor names it.
descriptions.workstations: A single station on a line.
descriptions.asset-types: The kind of machine: sewing, cutting, finishing, utility.
descriptions.asset-categories: A narrower grouping inside a type.
descriptions.failure-categories: The broad kind of fault: mechanical, electrical, operator.
descriptions.failure-codes: The specific fault, under its category.
descriptions.root-causes: What was found to be behind the fault.
descriptions.downtime-reason-codes: Why a machine was stopped, and whether that stoppage counts against availability.
descriptions.maintenance-types: Preventive, predictive, corrective — and whether each is planned work.
descriptions.meter-types: What is counted on a machine: running hours, stitches, cycles.
descriptions.warehouses: A store building on a factory site.
descriptions.stores: A store room inside a warehouse.
descriptions.bins: The shelf a part actually sits on. Every stock movement names one, so a company cannot receive a part until a bin exists.
descriptions.spare-part-categories: How the spare parts store is organised.
descriptions.item-departments: Where the library is kept and who is asked for it: Yarn Store, Garments Store, General Store. Not the organisation chart — that is Departments, above.
descriptions.item-categories: How the item library is organised: category, sub-category and detail category, three levels deep.
descriptions.cost-categories: What a cost was for, and which lifecycle bucket it rolls into.
descriptions.uoms: The units stock is counted in: pieces, kilograms, metres, rolls.
descriptions.uom-conversions: How one unit converts to another — a purchase in yards, stock in metres.
descriptions.hs-codes: Customs tariff codes with their duty and VAT rates, for imported items.
descriptions.fabric-defects: What a roll inspector can flag — Knit and Woven kept as separate lists.
descriptions.banks: Banks a supplier or the company holds an account with.
descriptions.payment-types: How money changes hands: cash, bank transfer, cheque, LC.
descriptions.gl-accounts: The chart of accounts stock and purchase postings map to. Structure now, real codes when finance signs off.
descriptions.grades: Pay and seniority grades, ranked by their order.
descriptions.designations: Job titles, with their department, employee category and grade.

descriptions.fabric-master: Fabric items a requisition may ask for — category, GSM, width, composition, colour and UOM.
descriptions.accessories-master: Labels, buttons, zippers and every other trim, with size, colour, UOM and specification.
descriptions.supplier-master: The suppliers the factory buys from — code, type, owner, address, VAT and TIN. Portal logins are linked to these.

fabric.title: Fabric items
fabric.subtitle: :active active of :count. Only active items appear on a new requisition.
fabric.required: Item code, name, category and UOM are required.

trims.title: Trims & accessories items
trims.subtitle: :active active of :count. Only active items appear on a new requisition.
trims.required: Item code, name, category and UOM are required.

supplier.title: Suppliers
supplier.subtitle: :active active of :count. Only active suppliers can be given a portal login.
supplier.required: Code, name and type are required.

master.code_taken: This code is already in use.

descriptions.create-requisition: Raise a material requisition by confirmed order or as a direct requisition — no supplier is chosen here.
descriptions.my-requisitions: Draft, submitted, rejected and approved requisitions, line by line.

pr.type_required: Choose Requisition by Order or Direct Requisition.
pr.order_required: Select the confirmed order this requisition is for.
pr.lines_required: Add at least one material line.
pr.line_qty: Line :n: Required qty must be a number greater than zero.
pr.line_uom_unknown: Line :n: :uom is not a unit of measure.
pr.locked: Only a draft requisition can be changed.
pr.delete_submitted: Submitted requisitions can never be deleted.

choose.by_order_line2: Buyer, style, order qty and delivery date fill in automatically
choose.direct_line2: Manual material requirement — your own details are captured automatically

form.hint_BY_ORDER: Order information comes from the confirmed order and cannot be edited here.
form.hint_DIRECT: No order information: a direct requisition carries only its own requirement.
form.order_hint: Choose an order to load its buyer, style, quantity and delivery date.
form.materials_hint: Pick items from master data. There is no supplier selection — every active supplier will be able to quote.
form.note_BY_ORDER: Order, item, quantity, UOM and requirement date are required.
form.note_DIRECT: No order information required — only the material requirement.

list.title: All requisitions
list.hint: Open a requisition to see its lines, quotations received and where each line stands.
list.delete_text: The draft and its lines are removed. Submitted requisitions can never be deleted.

descriptions.supplier-portal-access: Portal logins for suppliers: create an account and link it to the supplier it quotes for.

portal.title: Supplier portal logins
portal.active_n: :n active logins. Every supplier with an active login sees each submitted requirement and can quote on it.
portal.dialog_hint: The supplier signs in on the normal ERP login page and sees only the Supplier Portal.
portal.password_hint: At least 12 characters with upper and lower case, a digit and a symbol. Share it with the supplier securely.
portal.created: :email can now sign in to the Supplier Portal.
portal.email_taken: This email already has an account.

descriptions.supplier-dashboard: Open requirements, quotations submitted, revisions asked for and decisions.
descriptions.available-requirements: Fabric and accessories requirements open for quotation — quote a price, lead time and delivery.
descriptions.quotation-history: Your own quotations with every price revision, and negotiation requests to answer.

sp.for_suppliers: This screen is for supplier portal accounts. Ask the Super Admin for a supplier login.
sp.suppliers_only: Supplier accounts can only use the Supplier Portal.
sp.check_role: If you expected to see this screen, ask the Super Admin to check your role. Supplier accounts work from the Supplier Portal screens only.

req.title: Available requirements
req.hint: Requirements open to every active supplier. Quote a price, lead time and delivery date for the lines you can supply.
req.empty: No requirement is open for quotation.

form.note: Your price is visible only to the Super Admin. Other suppliers cannot see it, and once submitted it cannot be edited — a revised price is saved as a new revision.
form.revised: Revision :n of :no submitted — earlier prices are kept unchanged.

hist.title: Quotation history
hist.hint: Your quotations only, with every price revision you sent.

sp.no_login: This screen is for supplier portal accounts. Ask the Super Admin for a supplier login.
sp.qty_required: Quoted qty must be a number greater than zero.
sp.price_required: Unit price must be a number greater than zero.
sp.lead_required: Lead time is required, in whole days.
sp.line_closed: This requirement is no longer open for quotation.
sp.not_revisable: This quotation is :status and can no longer be revised.

descriptions.price-review: Compare every supplier's quotation per line, then reject, ask for negotiation, or approve and hand over.

review.title: Received quotations
review.confidential: Confidential: only the Super Admin and authorised approvers see supplier prices. Submitted prices cannot be edited or deleted.
review.no_quotes: No supplier has quoted on this line yet.
review.negotiate_hint: The supplier is asked for a revised price. Their new price is saved as a new revision; the current one is kept.
review.default_message: Please revise your quotation and submit your best possible price.
review.approve_hint: Select the follow-up merchandiser. The approved material, the supplier's full details and the delivery follow-up go to them.
review.reject_hint: The supplier is told the quotation was rejected, with your reason.
review.reject_line_hint: No supplier is chosen and every open quotation on the line is rejected.
review.negotiated: Negotiation requested — :supplier will be asked for a revised price.
review.wrong_status: This quotation is :status; it cannot be decided this way.

descriptions.assigned-materials: Approved materials handed to you — order, requisition, approval and supplier details, follow-ups and GRN.
descriptions.delivery-tracking: Every approved line's delivery status with required, received and balance quantity.

fu.hint: Click a line for its order, requisition, approval and supplier details and to log follow-ups.
fu.empty_mine: No approved material has been handed over to you yet.
fu.empty_all: No material has been approved yet.

f.payment_terms_value: As agreed on the purchase order

fu.fu_hint: Each entry's received quantity adds to the line's total. A receipt can be turned into a draft GRN for the store.

form.title: Add follow-up
form.balance: Balance :balance of :required. Received and balance quantities are worked out automatically.

grn.title: Raise GRN
grn.hint: Draft goods receipt for :qty :uom of :item from :supplier. It is verified and finalised onto stock on Merchandise Desk's receiving screen.

fu.tracking_hint: Balance = Required − Received, worked out from the follow-ups. Overdue next follow-ups are shown in red.
fu.closed: In-house — this line is closed; no more follow-ups are logged on it.
fu.over: Received qty cannot be more than the balance (:balance :uom).
fu.nothing_received: Nothing was received in this follow-up, so there is no goods receipt to raise.
fu.grn_raised: A goods receipt is already raised for this delivery: :no.
fu.currency: :currency receipts are not kept on Merchandise Desk; ask for the price in BDT, USD, EUR, CNY or INR.
fu.not_yours: Only the merchandiser this material was handed to logs its follow-ups.

audit.approved: Approved :qt (:supplier) for :item on :pr at :price (revision :revision); handed over to :to

descriptions.procurement-notifications: New requirements, quotations, revisions, approvals and handovers addressed to you.
descriptions.procurement-audit-trail: Every requisition, quotation, revision, decision, handover and follow-up — permanent and read-only.

ctl.audit_hint: Every critical transaction in this module. Entries are permanent and cannot be edited or deleted.

descriptions.procurement-dashboard: Requisitions, quotations, approvals and deliveries at a glance, and the workflow from master data to GRN.

dash.workflow_line: Master Data → Purchase Requisition (By Order / Direct) → All Suppliers → Quotation → Super Admin Review → Handover → Follow-up → GRN
dash.latest_hint: :items active items in master data · :with of :suppliers active suppliers have portal logins

fab.no_knit: No knitting or YD instruction has been written for this style yet.

svc.no_process: No process added — add dyeing, print, embroidery or wash.

yfm.no_fabric: Add the fabric on Fabrication first.
yfm.need: Pick the production category, item, garment part, fabric and garment colour.

ord.new_hint: Total price and lead time are derived from the quantity, the unit price and the two dates — they are never typed twice.
ord.sizes_hint: Pick an order to see its colour and size breakdown, adjust a quantity, or add a line.
ord.select_order_hint: Its colour × size lines open here.

oc.new_hint: One order is confirmed per style picked, numbered from the buyer's own series.
oc.pick_buyer: Pick the buyer to list their approved styles.
oc.no_styles: This buyer has no approved style yet.
oc.auto_hint: Read only — carried from the style.

oc.confirmed_hint: Numbered automatically per buyer and year — LPP-2026-000001.
oc.none: No order has been confirmed against this style yet.

sod.recent_styles_sub: The newest styles on either register.
sod.recent_orders_sub: The newest orders confirmed, numbered per buyer.

spb.caption: One row per style with its buyer, season, nature of work and how far its documents have got

fu.caption: Production progress per order: cutting, input, sewing, finishing and shipment against the order quantity

prj.empty_text: Rows appear here as the system records them.
prj.how: A projection is an order of type Projection — enter it on Order Register or confirm it on a style sheet; its call-offs are drawn here.
prj.call_offs_hint: Firm orders drawn down against the projection, never more than it projected.
prj.pick_hint: Its call-offs and balance open here.
prj.none: Nothing has been called off yet.

pck.need: Enter the SKU and pick the order, garment item and colour (or tick All Col?).
pck.no_orders: No order is confirmed against this style yet — confirm one on Order Confirmation.
pck.qty_hint: Qty is the packs the order needs: the pieces of that colour (from its size breakdown, or the whole order) over the pieces per pack.

fpr.new_hint: The five printed tabs — Knitting, Yarn Dyeing, AOP, Dyeing and Dyeing Finishing — are the category on this form.
fpr.pending_hint: Rates with no fibre combination template yet. Pick a chart category and assign each one its template.
fpr.none_pending: Every rate of this category has its template.

dsc.manage: Manage garment development styles and approval requests.
dsc.list_sub: Every style still in development, newest activity first.
dsc.inbox_sub: Development styles sent for approval. Every approver sees this same list.
dsc.sent_sub: Styles you sent for approval, and where each one stands.
dsc.sent_empty: You have not sent a style for approval yet.

wiz.save_first: Save the style profile first — the other steps open once the style exists.
wiz.locked_sent: This style is with its approver, so its profile and desks are closed to changes until it is approved, rejected or returned for revision.
wiz.locked_approved: This style has been approved. Its profile and desks are closed to changes.
wiz.image_after_save: Save the profile to attach the garment's image.
wiz.packing_hint: How every pack of this style is made up and cartoned.
wiz.pack_breakdown: Pack Breakdown — SKU, colour and pieces per pack, per item
wiz.attachments_hint: Views, tech pack, measurement sheet, fabric swatch and artwork. Stored on the server — the approver sees exactly these.

dlg.send_hint: Optional — anything the approver should know.
dlg.revision_hint: Say what needs changing. The merchandiser works from this note.
dlg.reject_hint: Say why the style is rejected.

srq.records_caption: Styles with their buyer, account, description, season, origin and status
srq.records_empty: No style has been raised yet.

srq.no_candidates: No development style is approved yet — approve one on the Development Style Catalogue.

srq.carried_hint: Carried from the approved development style — change it there and raise a change request.
srq.carried_none: The development style has nothing here yet.
srq.review_hint: Every step carries the approved development style; the profile is yours. Submit sends the request to its approver.
srq.reject_hint: Say why the request is rejected.
srq.sizes_hint: Pick a style to see the size sets it is offered in, and add another.
srq.pick_style_hint: Its size ranges load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.

sgl.empty_text: Rows appear here as the system records them.

emb.pending_hint: Rates still waiting on a decision, by buyer. Confirm one to make it costable, or drop it.
emb.pick_hint: Its rates load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
emb.confirm_text: The rate is confirmed and can be costed against. It can no longer be edited.
emb.drop_text: :type will be removed and the change recorded in the audit trail.
emb.footer: :n rate(s). Confirmed rates leave this list; they are on the records tab, where the screen refuses to rewrite them.
emb.none_pending: Nothing is waiting on a decision for this buyer.
emb.confirmed_help: Unconfirmed rates are what the Pendings tab lists.

cad.hint: Pick a CAD record to see its per-size marker consumption, and add a size.

cad.need: Enter the size and its consumption.

bgt.locked: This budget sheet is approved and locked for costing. Unlock it on the Budget Sheet Workflow to revise it.
bgt.title: Budget Sheet
bgt.subtitle: Key the order, budget each cost head against what was quoted, and build up the bill of material.
bgt.booking_later: Fabric Booking arrives with its own module (Merchandise Desk 06/11).

bgt.closed: FOB equals the sum of the heads — the costing is closed.
bgt.pick_order: Pick the style and its order to open its budget sheet.
bgt.per_piece: Every figure is per piece, in the order currency.

load.loaded: :n lines loaded from :from. Save to keep them.
load.none: Nothing to load: the order has no bulk fabric booking and its style no BOM.
load.replace: Lines loaded before are replaced; lines typed in are kept. Load now?
load.no_gsm: :fabric is booked in :unit without GSM and width, so its yarn stays in :unit.
load.auto_qty: Worked out from Cons/Dzn and Wastage %
load.booking_open: Open the fabric bookings of this order

bfb.hint: Key the order, then pair each dia-wise consumption with the garment quantity and colour it applies to.

bfb.empty: No booking has been raised yet.
bfb.delete_hint: The booking and its lines are removed.
bfb.grid_empty: Nothing added yet. Fill in both halves above and press Add to Grid.

bfb.no_cad: No CAD consumption has been recorded for that style yet.
bfb.no_lines: Add at least one line to the grid before saving.

afb.buyer_hint: Left empty, it follows the style's buyer account.

mai.health_table_hint: Every live order, weakest first, with the risk score it is read against

mai.prob_table_hint: Most likely to miss its date first, with the expected slip and the confidence behind it
mai.watch_hot_tail: are scoring 60 or above on this factor — the point at which it starts driving the composite rather than sitting inside it.
mai.worst_hint: The fifteen orders carrying the most :factor

material.title: Material Risk
material.hint: Booked and received fabric and trims read against what the order needs, and against how long is left
material.table_hint: Fabric and trim coverage against requirement, worst first

production.title: Production Risk
production.hint: Cutting, sewing and finishing output against the quantity ordered, read against the days remaining
production.table_hint: Floor progress against the days left before shipment, worst first

approval.title: Approval Risk
approval.hint: The approvals the order still needs — lab dips, samples, tests — weighted by how close production is to needing them.
approval.table_hint: Approvals outstanding against the production calendar, worst first

shipment.title: Shipment Risk

shipment.table_hint: Work left against days left, worst first

mai.drivers_hint: The four sub-scores averaged across the book — where the exposure actually sits

mai.expected_hint: Days each order is forecast to slip if nothing on it changes, longest first

mai.progress_hint: Production against the floor stages, task completion against the T&A calendar, and the next milestone

mai.tc_bands_hint: Closed against planned, across every live order's T&A calendar
mai.behind_hint: The fifteen orders with the least of their T&A closed
mai.tc_table_hint: Task completion beside production progress, with the next milestone and the forecast slip
mai.milestones_hint: The opening and closing events of each order's calendar, six weeks out

mai.dept_chart: Where the calendar stands, by department
mai.dept_chart_hint: Closed, still open and past plan — the twelve departments carrying the most overdue work
mai.dept_table_hint: Every T&A task on the live book grouped by the section that owns it, most overdue first
mai.pending_tasks_hint: Everything still open on a live order's calendar, earliest plan date first

mai.slip_chart_hint: Days each open task is forecast to push its order out by, largest first
mai.slip_table_hint: Every open task with the slip it is forecast to cause and how likely it is to cause it

mai.nothing_overdue: No T&A task is past its plan date.
mai.nothing_milestones: No milestone falls in the next six weeks.

numbering.intro: What this company's work orders, breakdowns and transfers are called.
numbering.reset_confirm: Go back to the platform default (:format)? It takes effect from the next period.
numbering.already_issued: {1} :count number already issued|[2,*] :count numbers already issued
numbering.next_period_notice: A change here renumbers nothing. Numbers already issued keep the shape they were given, and the new format takes effect when the counter next restarts — at the start of the next month or year.
numbering.gaps_note: Gaps in a run of numbers are normal. A number is allocated before the record is saved and is never reused, so a cancelled document leaves its number behind rather than passing it on.
numbering.saved: :type numbering saved. It takes effect from the next period.
numbering.reset_done: :type numbering is back to the platform default.
numbering.format_length: A format must be between 1 and 128 characters.
numbering.format_characters: A format may contain letters, digits, hyphens, slashes and full stops besides the placeholders.
numbering.sequence_required: The format must contain {SEQ}. Without the counter, every document in the period would be given the same number.
numbering.factory_required: This counter runs separately in each factory, so the format must contain {FACTORY}. Without it two factories would issue the same number on the same day.
numbering.month_required: This counter restarts each month, so the format must contain {MM} and {YYYY}. Without the month, January's first number and February's would be the same string.
numbering.month_not_allowed: This counter restarts once a year, so {MM} would put a month in the number that the counter does not follow.

mp.list_hint: Every version of every plan. Select a month and an order above to create one.
mp.info_hint: Read from the order book, the style sheet and the SMV / SAM master. Not editable here.
mp.tna_remark_none: No T&A calendar — activities use lead times
mp.no_smv: This order has no SMV on the SMV / SAM master or its style. Planning reads SMV from there — enter it at the source first.
mp.no_ship_date: This order has no shipment date. Enter it on the order first.
mp.cannot: This order cannot be planned yet
mp.cannot_hint: Fix the missing shipment date or SMV at its source, then come back.
mp.scenario_hint: Only the scenario on screen is saved.
mp.line_sel_hint: Status and free working days up to :date, the last sewing day before shipment.
mp.no_free: No free working day before the deadline
mp.input_hint: Fetched from the line master. Adjust what is different for this order; capacity recalculates at once.
mp.tick_lines: Tick one or more lines under Line Selection.
mp.no_line_hint: Select one or more available lines to calculate the plan.
mp.shortfall_body: :qty PCS cannot be scheduled before :date on the chosen lines — add a line or adjust the resources.
mp.late: Sewing runs past :date — shipment on :ship is at risk.
mp.lead_passed_body: :list should have started before today to meet this production start.
mp.lead_hint: From Planning Setup. The activities count back from cutting and forward from the last sewing day.
mp.result_hint: Holidays and days other orders hold are skipped. Sewing must end by :date for shipment on :ship.
mp.result_empty: Select lines, check their resources and press Calculate Plan to lay out the production schedule and daily targets.
mp.remarks_ph: Anything the planning manager should know before confirming…
mp.save_first: Save the plan first; it can be confirmed once saved.
mp.confirm_body: Confirming locks the plan. Its lines, resources, capacity, dates, targets and activities become the original commitment.
mp.delete_body: The draft and its layout are removed. A locked version is not touched.
mp.locked_banner: This master plan is locked and cannot be modified. Daily plans and actual output are recorded beside it, never over it. For a change, raise a revision request — the approved revision becomes V:next.
mp.revised_banner: A later version has been locked over this one; it is kept for the record.

fc.title: Master Plan Updated (Current Forecast)
fc.hint: Original plan, progress to date and expected completion — the original plan is never overwritten.
fc.risk_note: Current forecast may affect the confirmed shipment date. :qty PCS more capacity is needed before :date.
fc.ok_note: Forecast from today at the planned line capacity on free working days; a day with a daily plan counts its target.

rev.none: No revision has been requested on this version.
rev.req_body: The locked plan stays in force. If the planning manager approves, the next version opens as a draft copied from this one.
rev.reason_ph: e.g. Line-03 down for maintenance from 12-Mar; buyer moved shipment; quantity increased…
rev.approve_body: Approve this revision? The next version opens as a draft; the locked version stays in force until it is confirmed. The decision is recorded in the audit trail.
rev.reject_body: The locked plan stays as it is. Say why — the requester sees it.
rev.title: Requests to change a locked master plan, and what the planning manager decided
rev.empty: No revision request has been raised yet.

daily.add_ph: Add another line to the day…

daily.fc_hint: How the order stands after the days recorded so far. The master plan itself is not changed.

v.reason: Give the reason for the change.
v.revision_open: A revision of :no is already open.
v.decided: This request has already been decided.

platform.tenants_intro: Every company on this installation, their contracts and their size.
platform.no_data_access_note: Counts and contracts only. Seeing a customer's machines, work orders or breakdowns requires an audited support grant, and the customer is told when one is opened.
platform.company_code_hint: Appears inside every work order and breakdown number this customer will ever issue. Short, and hard to change afterwards.
platform.no_tenants_hint: Create the first one to get started.
platform.new_tenant_intro: Creates the company, its first factory and its owner account together. All three are needed before anybody can sign in and do anything.
platform.first_factory_hint: Machines live in a factory, document numbers are issued per factory, and the working calendar hangs off it. A company without one cannot be used. More can be added by the customer.
platform.owner_hint: The first person who can sign in. They get the Company Owner role, company-wide, and can invite everybody else.
platform.owner_credentials_once: Give these to the customer now. The password is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
platform.code_taken: That code is already in use, including by a deleted company.
platform.owner_email_taken: An account with this email already exists. Adding an existing person to a new company is a different operation — do it from the company's own user screen after a support grant.
platform.no_contract_yet: No contract has been recorded for this customer yet.
platform.new_contract_hint: Saving supersedes the current contract rather than editing it: an invoice already raised under the old terms has been sent to somebody, and changing what it was calculated from makes it unexplainable.
platform.contract_saved: Contract saved. The previous one has been archived.
platform.auto_renew: Renew automatically at the end of the term
platform.suspend_confirm: Suspend this customer? Everybody is signed out and nobody can sign in until it is reversed. No data is deleted.
platform.suspended: :name has been suspended. Their data is untouched.
platform.support_access_hint: Seeing a customer's data requires a reason, expires by itself, and is announced to the customer. You then act as one of their users, which means you see exactly what that person sees and no more.
platform.reason_example: Ticket 4471: work orders not appearing after a factory transfer.
platform.reason_too_short: Write a real reason. It goes to the customer and into the audit log.
platform.support_opened: Access opened. The customer has been notified.
platform.no_grants: Nobody has been given access to this customer.
platform.grant_not_active: That access has ended or expired. Open a new one.
platform.not_a_member: That person is not an active member of this company.
platform.support_session_banner: Support session — you are inside a customer's account
platform.growth_chart_label: New customers by month, the last six months
platform.limits_are_advisory: Recorded for billing. Nothing is blocked when a customer goes over.
platform.limits_are_enforced: Enforced. At the limit, adding another factory, machine or user is refused. Anything already over the limit is left alone — only the next one is stopped.
platform.supersedes_notice: Saving this archives :number. Invoices already raised under it are left alone.
platform.act_as_hint: Whoever you pick is named in the audit log. Acting as the owner and acting as a storekeeper are different amounts of access.
platform.currently_suspended: This company is suspended. Nobody in it can sign in.
platform.suspend_hint: Stops everybody in this company from signing in. Nothing is deleted, and reactivating restores access immediately.
platform.suspension_reason_hint: Shown to the customer word for word on the screen that tells them they are stopped.
platform.suspension_reason_example: Invoice INV-2026-0042 unpaid since 30 June, after three reminders.
platform.no_invoices_hint: Raise one below, or let the scheduled run issue the first on the billing cycle.
platform.invoice_drafted: Invoice :number drafted. Check it, then issue it.
platform.no_contract_to_invoice: This customer has no contract, so there is nothing to invoice against. Record a contract first.
platform.code_is_fixed: The code :code cannot be changed. It is inside every work order and breakdown number this customer has issued.
platform.reset_hint: Signs the account out everywhere and stops its API tokens. The new password is shown once, here.
platform.reset_confirm: Issue a new password for :name? They are signed out everywhere immediately.
platform.reset_shown_once: Give this to the customer now. It is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
platform.password_reset_done: A new password has been issued for :name.
platform.reset_reason_example: Owner locked out; company email account closed. Ticket 5120.
platform.credential_change_notice: The :what for :account was changed by support. Reason: :reason
platform.customer_login_hint: The owner account — the one the customer signs in with, and the only one nobody inside their company can reset. Both changes are announced to the customer and recorded in the audit log.
platform.customer_id_hint: This is what they type to sign in. Change it when the address was mistyped or the mailbox is gone.
platform.limits_hint: What this customer is allowed. Changing these does not change their contract, its price or its term.
platform.limits_blank_hint: Leave a box empty for no limit.
platform.limits_need_contract: Limits live on the contract, so this customer needs one before limits can be set.
platform.overage_effect: Only Block actually stops anything: at the limit, adding another is refused. Warn only and Allow and bill let the work carry on and settle it commercially.
platform.domain_none: This customer uses the shared address. Add one below to give them their own.
platform.domain_host_hint: For a subdomain, type only the first part — it is added to :base. For their own domain, type the whole address.
platform.domain_remove_confirm: Remove :host? Anybody using it will have to go back to the shared address.
platform.domain_added: :host has been added. It will not work until the records below are in place.
platform.domain_primary_set: :host is now the address this customer is given.
platform.domain_taken: That address is already in use by a customer.
platform.domain_invalid: That does not look like a web address.
platform.domain_verify_first: An address has to be working before it can be the primary one.
platform.domain_not_found_yet: The record is not visible yet. DNS changes can take a few hours to spread — try again later.
platform.domain_verify_first_note: Until this is done the address does not reach anybody, which is deliberate: honouring an unproven claim would let one customer collect another's sign-ins.
platform.domain_steps: What the customer has to do
platform.domain_step_cname: Add a CNAME record pointing their address at ours:
platform.domain_step_txt: Add a TXT record proving they own it:
platform.domain_step_check: Then press Check now. DNS changes can take a few hours to spread.
platform.domain_tls_note: A new address also needs an HTTPS certificate on the server. That is done by the server, not from this screen — see docs/11-Deployment.md.
platform.support_desk_intro: Who is inside a customer's data, and who has been.
platform.support_none_open: Nobody has access to a customer's data.
platform.support_no_history: No support access has been opened
platform.support_no_history_hint: Every grant ever opened is listed here, with who opened it and why.
platform.notifications_intro: What the rest of the platform staff have done.
platform.notifications_empty_hint: Support access, suspensions and closures appear here as they happen.
platform.notify_erased: :name erased :company and all of its data
platform.close_hint: Ends the account. Everybody in this company is signed out and cannot sign in again, and the customer disappears from the list above.
platform.close_reversible: Nothing is deleted. A closed account can be reopened, and everything in it comes back exactly as it was.
platform.confirm_code_label: Type the customer code :code to confirm
platform.confirm_code_mismatch: That is not the customer code. Type :code exactly.
platform.closed_done: :name has been closed. It can still be reopened from the list.
platform.closed_customers_hint: Closed accounts keep all their data and can be reopened. Erasing one is permanent.
platform.erase_hint: Deletes this customer and everything in it — machines, work orders, breakdowns, stock, invoices and users' access. This cannot be undone.
platform.erase_no_export: There is no tenant export yet, so nothing is kept. If the customer may ever ask for their records back, reopen the account instead.
platform.erase_audit_kept: The audit log survives: what was done, by whom and when is kept even after the data it describes is gone.
platform.erased_done: :name and all of its data have been erased.
platform.finance_intro: What each customer has paid, what is still owed, and what running the platform costs.
platform.refunded_note: Includes :amount :currency refunded, already taken off the received figure.
platform.no_money_by_month: Nothing has been received or spent in the last twelve months.
platform.no_money_yet_hint: Once a customer has a contract and an invoice, the totals appear here.
platform.no_billed_customers_hint: Give a customer a contract, then raise their first invoice from their Billing tab.
platform.nothing_overdue_hint: Every issued invoice is either paid or still inside its due date.
platform.no_payments_hint: Each payment recorded against an invoice appears here, newest first.
platform.expense_remove_confirm: Remove this cost from the totals?
platform.no_expenses_hint: Hosting, domains, software and the rest. Without them the net figure is only income.
platform.edit_company_hint: The customer's own details. Their code is fixed and cannot be changed here.
platform.logo_hint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 512 KB. Shown at 120×120.
platform.no_usage_history: No usage has been measured yet. The first month appears after billing:advance next runs.
platform.tickets_intro: Ask the provider something, in writing.
platform.tickets_desk_intro: Every customer's tickets, in one inbox.
platform.ticket_opened: Ticket opened. The provider has been told.
platform.ticket_closed: This ticket is closed. Open a new one to raise it again.
platform.ticket_status_invalid: That is not a valid status.
platform.ticket_priority_invalid: That is not a valid priority.
platform.ticket_category_invalid: That is not a valid category.
platform.ticket_no_longer_editable: This ticket can no longer be edited — someone has already replied.
platform.ticket_no_longer_deletable: This ticket can no longer be deleted — someone has already replied.
platform.no_tickets_hint: This customer has not raised anything with the provider.
platform.no_tickets_hint_tenant: When something needs the provider's attention, raise it here.
platform.tickets_no_closed_hint: Every ticket, once it is answered and closed, is listed here.

descriptions.requisition-column-setup: The requisition columns, their formulas and colours, and which columns belong to Knit or Woven.
descriptions.acc-budget-column-setup: The accessories BOM worksheet: its columns, formulas and colours, and the Unit Cost Rules that work out Cost/Pc for each unit.
descriptions.master-data: The module's own lists: Accessories Item and the requisition's Order Type, Item, Wash Type, Fabric Type, Fabric Composition, GSM, Sustainability, Parts, Yarn Type, Yarn Count, Yarn Composition and Additional Process.
descriptions.accessory-items: Accessories a BOM line picks: code, name, category and the unit they are usually bought in.
descriptions.yarn-types: Yarn types a knit requisition line asks for.
descriptions.wash-types: Garment washes a requisition line names.
descriptions.additional-processes: Extra fabric or garment processes a requisition line names.
descriptions.gsm: Fabric weights a requisition line picks. Pre-Budget keeps its own list, apart from Order Summary.
descriptions.sustainability: Certified fibre programmes (BCI, GOTS and others). Pre-Budget keeps its own list.
descriptions.order-types: Order types (Confirmed PO, BLOCK, Buying File and others). Pre-Budget keeps its own list.
descriptions.items: Garment items a requisition line picks (Dress, Polo, T-Shirt …), as Norban lists them.
descriptions.fabric-types: Fabric types a requisition line picks (Single Jersey, Brush Back Fleece, 2X2 Rib …).
descriptions.fabric-compositions: The fabric's fibre mix as written (95% Cotton 5% Elastane …).
descriptions.parts: Garment parts a fabric goes into (Body, Neck Rib, Armhole Binding + Neck …).
descriptions.yarn-counts: Yarn counts a knit requisition line picks (30/1 Ne, 28S, 40D, 100D/36F …).
descriptions.yarn-compositions: The yarn as Norban writes it (Siro 50/50 [ 50% BCI Cotton-50% Recycled Polyester ] …).

acc.title: Accessories Items
acc.subtitle: :active active of :count.
acc.required: Name is required. A blank code gets the next ACC number.

master.name_taken: This name is already in the list.

descriptions.dashboard: The module at a glance: requisitions, quantity and FOB value, the budgets by status, the work still open, buyers and delivery months, and the latest saves.

descriptions.column-setup: The requisition columns, their formulas and colours, and which columns belong to Knit or Woven.
descriptions.create-budget: Make a pre-budget from completed requisitions of one buyer, or open one by its number: yarn and fabric lines, supplier prices, FOB and costs.

descriptions.stock-yarn-declaration: Local and import yarn and fabric a budget uses from stock, ready to print.

descriptions.budget-finalized: Budgets sent for approval (Merchandising Head → CFO → MD): waiting, approved, sent back, revised. Open one to see it whole and approve, withdraw or revise it.
descriptions.budget-overview: Each budget orders at a glance: style, colours and size range, quantity, FOB and RFI/SD date, under Buyer - Brand - Season - Factory. Print on A4.
